notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). No ROS graph, rosbridge connection, FlightForge/Unity simulator, GPU rendering or hardware run was performed or is claimed; the package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null). The pinned clone was left unmodified at e4715a8c75aac70a9bcd7f75113746b938139117; no network, pip install or upstream execution was used. SHAPE AND SCOPE: a configuration-only ROS 2 RosDriver over rosbridge, mode simulated, risk R0, device_kind world.sim; no Python native class and no native.py. The package binds the two always-published observation topics of the pinned FlightforgeSimulator component under its shipped launch: /clock (rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock, remapped from ~/clock_out at launch/flightforge_simulator.launch.py:120 and published at src/flightforge_simulator.cpp:1185 and 1320-1333) and /flightforge_simulator/uav_poses (geometry_msgs/msg/PoseArray, remapped from ~/uav_poses_out at launch/flightforge_simulator.launch.py:121 and published at src/flightforge_simulator.cpp:1187 and 2412-2441). The launch node is named flightforge_simulator in an empty namespace (launch/flightforge_simulator.launch.py:110-111), so the private ~/uav_poses remap resolves to /flightforge_simulator/uav_poses; the upstream tokens are recorded as source_name. A deployment that changes the node name or namespace must expose the declared absolute endpoints. The resource snapshot is empty (no parameters/reads); both observations are explicit subscriptions, not automatic snapshots. SAFETY AND NOT COVERED: the pinned clone creates no ROS service or action server for flight control, pause, reset or stop. The only pause path is the dynamic parameter mrs_uav_flightforge_simulator/paused (registered at src/flightforge_simulator.cpp:740; callbackPause cancels timer_main_ and timer_status_ at 2111-2129); ROS parameter access is not a rosbridge opcode and the clone does not declare the parameter-service type, so no source-cited stop binding is possible. A RosDriver profile that publishes the UAV command topics would therefore be unconfirmed at the stock e-stop (SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED), and the package does not expose them. This observation-only profile has no native stop; the stock e-stop latches it and reports software_only. The extension observation capabilities remain latched after the e-stop even though their verb is read. NOT COVERED: the UAV attitude/velocity/position/tracker command topics consumed by the external mrs_multirotor_simulator stack; the hw_api plugin and arming/offboard callbacks; per-UAV odom/imu/rangefinder topics; lidar, RGB/stereo/depth images and camera_info; TF; world step/reset/seed/snapshot; the external Unity binary; any physical stop. No Limit is declared because no action has a numeric input and the clone states no numeric bound for these observation topics; consequently site-limits.example.json is not needed. FAKE AND FIDELITY: fake.py is a ROS-free mhs.bridge.ros_transport.RecordingRosTransport contract fake with canned placeholder replies, not captured traffic and not the FlightForge/Unity simulator. Every fake number is marked # placeholder. It answers one /clock sample and one one-pose /flightforge_simulator/uav_poses sample; it runs no Unity process, physics, sensors, renderer, wall-clock loop or ROS graph. Fidelity is F0 for the deployed fake: engine analytic:ROS-free contract fake with canned placeholder replies (no physics), determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0 (no pacing), reset none, no snapshot/restore. The upstream 100 Hz simulation and 400 Hz clock rates are source facts only. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six package cases: clock observation, pose observation, wire subscriptions/types, silent clock deadline failure, malformed clock refusal, and the e-stop latch on the extension observation. Warnings kept: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected because no actuating capability declares a limit; every other CL3 test passed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were emitted. Last gate run: G1-G9 pass with G8 warn, exit 0, digest sha256:2f76881eb01cede69cb14e5756945778efdf407273021a0ce30099c9e003e8bf; check-report.json is the gate's own report.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the /clock and /flightforge_simulator/uav_poses bindings (private ~/clock_out and ~/uav_poses_out publishers of the component that the launch names flightforge_simulator in an empty namespace, remapped to /clock and ~/uav_poses: src/flightforge_simulator.cpp:1185-1187, launch/flightforge_simulator.launch.py:110-121), the ROS 2 Clock and PoseArray output schemas, the software-only e-stop of this observation-only R0 profile, the fake, the tests and all 14 facts against the pin. The package called the external simulator a Unity binary in its docstring, safe_state, fidelity notes and gaps, although the node connects to an Unreal Engine game through ueds_connector ('Unreal's game mode controller', 894-905); it said the flight-command topics are consumed by an external stack, while UavSystemRos objects that the node itself constructs consume them and the clone's hw_api plugin publishes them (872-888, launch/hw_api.launch.py:110-124); and three facts claimed more than their lines (a 'false default' that reads an API outside the clone, an ordering against publishers outside the cited line, and a 'not a limit' remark on the config rates). The reviewer corrected the docstring, safe_state, fidelity notes and gaps and those three facts, added eight facts (publishPoses only after a simulation step, the UavSystemRos construction, the unbounded FlightForge connection loop that precedes the publishers, the publisher and main-timer creation, the hw_api command remaps, the flag-only arming callback, and the licence conflict of a GPL-2.0 LICENSE with BSD 3-Clause in package.xml) and a gap stating that both topics stay silent until the binary is connected and while paused (driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:2f76881eb01cede69cb14e5756945778efdf407273021a0ce30099c9e003e8bf); the author's RESULT.json notes still say 'FlightForge/Unity' and that an external stack consumes the commands, which this review corrects. For the human reviewer: Observation-only simulator endpoint at R0; nothing in this package stops a UAV. The clock and pose topics exist only after the node has connected to the FlightForge (Unreal Engine) binary on localhost:8551, which timerInit retries every second without a limit, and both go silent while the dynamic parameter paused is true. The per-UAV command interfaces under /flightforge_simulator/<uav_name>/ and the hw_api plugin are not covered; the plugin's arming callback only stores a flag and answers success, so a disarm is not a stop. The shipped tmux session (tmux/one_drone/session.yml) also starts the MRS UAV core, automatic start and a takeoff script. Licence conflict inside the clone: LICENSE is GPL-2.0 while package.xml says BSD 3-Clause, and the card says publish_review not_required; the owner decides before publication.
